about: Milestones in spaceflight and space science, 1903 to 2026. agencies: nasa, ussr (Soviet Union / Roscosmos), esa, cnsa, isro, jaxa, spacex, other. Images reuse sources listed in gallery.json.

ussr.label: Soviet Union / Roscosmos
ussr.full: Soviet space programme and Russia's State Space Corporation (Roscosmos)

cnsa.label: China (CNSA)
cnsa.full: China National Space Administration (CNSA) and China Manned Space Agency (CMSA)

jaxa.label: Japan (JAXA)
jaxa.full: Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) and its predecessors

other.label: Other
other.full: Other agencies, companies and science collaborations

decades.1900: Theory first: the mathematics of the rocket.
decades.1940: Weapons reach space, and cameras ride along.
decades.1960: From the first orbit to the Moon in eight years.
decades.1970: Stations, rovers and the grand tour of the planets.
decades.1980: The Shuttle era, and what it cost.
decades.1990: Great observatories and a shared station.
decades.2000: A permanent human presence, and private pioneers.
decades.2020: Commercial crews and the return to the Moon.

events.title: Tsiolkovsky publishes the rocket equation
events.description: Konstantin Tsiolkovsky's paper 'The Exploration of Cosmic Space by Means of Reaction Devices' showed how a rocket's change in speed depends on its exhaust velocity and the ratio of its fuelled to empty mass. He proposed liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen as propellants, decades before anyone could build such a rocket.

events.title: Goddard flies the first liquid-fuelled rocket
events.description: In a snowy field in Auburn, Massachusetts, Robert Goddard launched a rocket burning gasoline and liquid oxygen. It flew for 2.5 seconds, rising 12.5 m (41 ft) and landing 56 m (184 ft) away, but it proved the technology almost every orbital launcher still uses.

events.title: A V-2 becomes the first object in space
events.description: A German V-2 test rocket, MW 18014, was launched vertically from Peenemünde and reached about 176 km, crossing the Kármán line into space. The V-2 was a weapon built with forced labour, and after the war its engineers and hardware seeded both the American and Soviet rocket programmes.

events.title: First photograph from space
events.description: A captured V-2 launched from New Mexico carried a 35 mm movie camera to about 105 km (65 miles). The film survived the crash in a steel cassette and gave humanity its first look at Earth from space.
events.imageCredit: U.S. Army / White Sands Missile Range / APL

events.title: Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite
events.description: The Soviet Union launched a 58 cm (23 in) polished sphere whose radio beeps could be picked up by amateurs around the world. Its success shocked the United States and started the Space Race.

events.title: Laika orbits Earth
events.description: Sputnik 2 carried Laika, a stray dog from the streets of Moscow, making her the first animal to orbit Earth. She died within hours from overheating, but the flight showed a living creature could survive launch and weightlessness.

events.title: Explorer 1 finds the Van Allen belts
events.description: America's first satellite, built by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) and launched by the Army, carried James Van Allen's cosmic-ray detector. It discovered belts of charged particles trapped by Earth's magnetic field, the first major scientific discovery of the Space Age.

events.title: NASA opens its doors
events.description: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) began operations, absorbing the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA) and its roughly 8,000 employees. It gave the United States a single civilian agency for exploring space.

events.title: Luna 2 reaches the Moon
events.description: Luna 2 struck the Moon near the crater Archimedes, the first human-made object to reach another celestial body. On the way it confirmed that the Moon has no significant magnetic field.

events.title: Luna 3 photographs the far side
events.description: Swinging behind the Moon, Luna 3 photographed about 70 percent of the side never visible from Earth, developing the film on board and scanning it for transmission. The far side turned out to have almost none of the dark lava plains of the near side.

events.title: Yuri Gagarin, first human in space
events.description: Yuri Gagarin completed one orbit of Earth in Vostok 1 in 108 minutes. As planned, he ejected from the capsule at about 7 km and landed separately by parachute.

events.title: Alan Shepard, first American in space
events.description: Alan Shepard flew a 15-minute suborbital arc in the Mercury capsule Freedom 7. Unlike Gagarin, he took manual control of his spacecraft's orientation during the flight.

events.title: Kennedy sets the Moon goal
events.description: Before a joint session of Congress, President John F. Kennedy committed the nation to landing a man on the Moon and returning him safely before the decade was out. At that moment the United States had flown one astronaut, for 15 minutes.

events.title: John Glenn orbits Earth
events.description: John Glenn circled Earth three times in Friendship 7, the first American in orbit. A faulty sensor suggested his heat shield was loose, so he kept the retrorocket pack strapped on during re-entry; the shield was fine.

events.title: Mariner 2 flies past Venus
events.description: Mariner 2 made the first successful flyby of another planet. It measured a surface far hotter than expected, ending hopes of a temperate Venus.

events.title: Valentina Tereshkova, first woman in space
events.description: A textile worker and amateur parachutist, Valentina Tereshkova orbited Earth 48 times in almost three days aboard Vostok 6. She logged more time in space on that one flight than all the Mercury astronauts combined.

events.title: Alexei Leonov, first spacewalk
events.description: Alexei Leonov floated outside Voskhod 2 for about 12 minutes. His suit ballooned in the vacuum and he could only squeeze back into the airlock after bleeding off some of its pressure.

events.title: Mariner 4, first close-ups of Mars
events.description: Mariner 4 flew past Mars and returned 21 complete pictures, the first close-up images of another planet. They showed a cratered, Moon-like surface, ending popular dreams of canals and vegetation.

events.title: Gemini 6A and 7 meet in orbit
events.description: Gemini 6A pulled within about 30 cm (1 ft) of Gemini 7, the first rendezvous of two crewed spacecraft. Meeting up in orbit was essential to the lunar-orbit plan chosen for Apollo.

events.title: Luna 9 lands softly on the Moon
events.description: Luna 9 made the first soft landing on another world and sent back panoramas of the lunar surface. It proved the ground was firm enough to support a spacecraft, not a sea of deep dust.

events.title: Gemini 8, the first docking
events.description: Neil Armstrong and David Scott docked with an uncrewed Agena target, the first docking of two spacecraft. A stuck thruster then sent them tumbling at nearly one turn per second, and Armstrong's calm recovery helped earn him command of Apollo 11.

events.title: The Apollo 1 fire
events.description: A fire in the pure-oxygen cabin during a launch-pad test killed Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee. The redesign that followed, with a quick-opening hatch and non-flammable materials, made the Apollo spacecraft far safer.

events.title: Soyuz 1 and Vladimir Komarov
events.description: Vladimir Komarov died when the parachutes of Soyuz 1 failed to open properly during landing, the first in-flight death of the space age. Soyuz was redesigned, and descendants of the spacecraft still fly today.

events.title: Apollo 8 circles the Moon
events.description: Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders became the first people to leave Earth orbit, orbiting the Moon ten times over Christmas Eve. Their Earthrise photograph and Christmas Eve broadcast reached one of the largest audiences in history.

events.title: Apollo 11: humans walk on the Moon
events.description: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed the lunar module Eagle in the Sea of Tranquillity while Michael Collins orbited overhead. Armstrong's first step was watched live by an estimated 600 million people.

events.title: Ohsumi, Japan's first satellite
events.description: On its fifth attempt, the University of Tokyo's Lambda 4S rocket put the small Ohsumi satellite into orbit. Japan became the fourth country to launch a satellite on its own rocket.

events.title: Apollo 13: 'Houston, we've had a problem'
events.description: An oxygen tank exploded about 56 hours into the flight, crippling the service module on the way to the Moon. Jim Lovell, Jack Swigert and Fred Haise used the lunar module as a lifeboat and splashed down safely on 17 April.

events.title: Dong Fang Hong 1, China's first satellite
events.description: A Long March 1 rocket launched Dong Fang Hong 1, which broadcast the song 'The East Is Red' from orbit. China became the fifth country to launch a satellite on its own rocket.

events.title: Luna 16 brings Moon rock home
events.description: Luna 16 landed in the Sea of Fertility, drilled up 101 g of soil and launched it back to Earth, where it landed on 24 September. It was the first robotic sample return from another world.

events.title: Lunokhod 1, the first planetary rover
events.description: Lunokhod 1, an eight-wheeled rover driven remotely by a team on Earth, became the first robot to rove another world. It travelled about 10.5 km over nearly eleven months.

events.title: Venera 7 signals from Venus
events.description: Venera 7 transmitted from the surface of Venus for about 23 minutes, the first signals ever received from the surface of another planet. It reported a temperature of about 475 °C (887 °F).

events.title: Salyut 1, the first space station
events.description: The Soviet Union launched Salyut 1, the world's first space station. Its only crew, arriving on Soyuz 11 in June, lived aboard for 23 days.

events.title: The Soyuz 11 crew is lost
events.description: Georgy Dobrovolsky, Vladislav Volkov and Viktor Patsayev died when a valve opened and their capsule depressurised before re-entry. They remain the only people to die above the Kármán line, and cosmonauts have worn pressure suits for launch and landing ever since.

events.title: Mariner 9 orbits Mars
events.description: Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit another planet, arriving during a global dust storm. When the dust cleared it mapped giant volcanoes and the canyon system later named Valles Marineris in its honour.

events.title: Pioneer 10 heads for Jupiter
events.description: Pioneer 10 launched toward the first crossing of the asteroid belt and the first flyby of Jupiter, in December 1973. It carries a plaque showing who sent it and from where, in case anyone ever finds it.

events.title: Apollo 17, the last Moon landing so far
events.description: Gene Cernan and geologist Harrison Schmitt spent three days exploring the Taurus–Littrow valley while Ron Evans orbited above; on the way out the crew took the Blue Marble photograph. Cernan's footprints, left on 14 December 1972, are still the last made by a human on the Moon.

events.title: Skylab, America's first space station
events.description: Skylab was built from a spare Saturn V third stage and launched on the last Saturn V to fly. Three crews lived aboard for up to 84 days, studying the Sun and the effects of long-duration weightlessness.

events.title: The European Space Agency is founded
events.description: Ten European countries merged the European Space Research Organisation (ESRO) and the European Launcher Development Organisation (ELDO) into the European Space Agency (ESA). It now has 23 member states.

events.title: Apollo–Soyuz: a handshake in orbit
events.description: An American Apollo and a Soviet Soyuz docked, and commanders Tom Stafford and Alexei Leonov shook hands through the open hatch. The mission eased Cold War tensions and set a precedent for the International Space Station.

events.title: Venera 9: first pictures from another planet's surface
events.description: Venera 9 landed on Venus and returned the first photographs taken on the surface of another planet. The black-and-white panorama showed flat, angular rocks under a surprisingly bright sky.

events.title: Viking 1 lands on Mars
events.description: Viking 1 became the first spacecraft to land on Mars and operate successfully, sending its first picture within minutes. Its biology experiments tested the soil for signs of life, with results still debated today.

events.title: The Voyagers launch
events.description: Voyager 2 launched on 20 August and Voyager 1 on 5 September 1977, exploiting a rare alignment of the outer planets. Between them they visited Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, and both have now crossed into interstellar space.

events.title: Ariane 1 gives Europe its own rocket
events.description: The first Ariane rocket lifted off from Kourou, French Guiana, giving Europe independent access to space. The Ariane family went on to launch a large share of the world's commercial satellites.

events.title: India reaches orbit with SLV-3
events.description: The Satellite Launch Vehicle (SLV-3), whose project director was A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, placed the Rohini satellite in orbit from Sriharikota. India became the seventh country to reach orbit with its own rocket.

events.title: STS-1: the first Space Shuttle flight
events.description: Twenty years to the day after Gagarin, John Young and Robert Crippen flew Columbia into orbit, the first time a crewed spacecraft carried people on its very first launch. The Shuttle flew 135 missions over the next 30 years.

events.title: Sally Ride, first American woman in space
events.description: Physicist Sally Ride flew aboard Challenger on STS-7 and operated the Shuttle's robotic arm to release and recapture a satellite. She later served on the boards investigating both Shuttle disasters.

events.title: Bruce McCandless flies free
events.description: Using the nitrogen-jet Manned Maneuvering Unit (MMU), Bruce McCandless flew about 98 m (320 ft) from Challenger with no tether, the first untethered spacewalk. The photograph of him alone against the black of space became an icon.

events.title: The Challenger disaster
events.description: Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after launch when an O-ring seal in a solid rocket booster failed in unusually cold weather, killing all seven crew, including teacher Christa McAuliffe. The Rogers Commission faulted both the joint design and NASA's decision-making.

events.title: Mir's core module reaches orbit
events.description: Mir was the first station assembled from modules in orbit, growing over ten years. It hosted crews almost continuously until 1999, including Valeri Polyakov's record 437-day stay, and was deorbited in 2001.

events.title: Giotto meets Halley's Comet
events.description: ESA's Giotto flew within about 600 km of the nucleus of Halley's Comet, returning the first close-up images of a comet's nucleus. It revealed a dark, potato-shaped body venting jets of gas and dust.

events.title: Voyager 2 reaches Neptune
events.description: Voyager 2 skimmed about 4,950 km above Neptune's cloud tops, the final planetary encounter of its grand tour. It found the Great Dark Spot and active plumes on the moon Triton.

events.title: The Pale Blue Dot
events.description: At Carl Sagan's urging, Voyager 1 turned its camera back from about 6 billion km and photographed Earth as a speck in a sunbeam. They were among the last images Voyager 1 ever took.

events.title: Hubble launches, with a flaw
events.description: Space Shuttle Discovery carried the Hubble Space Telescope into orbit. Its first images were blurred because the main mirror had been ground to the wrong shape, off by about 2.2 micrometres at its edge.

events.title: Astronauts fix Hubble
events.description: On STS-61, astronauts made five spacewalks to install corrective optics and a new Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2. Hubble's vision was restored, and it went on to transform almost every field of astronomy.

events.title: 51 Pegasi b, a planet around a Sun-like star
events.description: Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz announced the first planet found orbiting a Sun-like star, a 'hot Jupiter' that circles it every 4.2 days. The discovery overturned ideas about how planetary systems form and won the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics.

events.title: Galileo arrives at Jupiter
events.description: Galileo became the first spacecraft to orbit Jupiter, and its probe plunged into the planet's atmosphere the same day. Over eight years it found strong evidence of a salty ocean under the ice of Europa.

events.title: Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner
events.description: Mars Pathfinder bounced to a landing on airbags and released Sojourner, the first rover on Mars. The low-cost mission drew record crowds to NASA's websites and set the pattern for later rovers.

events.title: Zarya: the ISS begins
events.description: Zarya, a Russian-built module funded by the United States, was the first piece of the International Space Station (ISS) to reach orbit. Weeks later Space Shuttle Endeavour attached the American Unity node.

events.title: Expedition 1: humans move in for good
events.description: Bill Shepherd, Yuri Gidzenko and Sergei Krikalev became the first long-term crew of the International Space Station. People have lived in space continuously ever since.

events.title: Dennis Tito, the first space tourist
events.description: American businessman Dennis Tito paid a reported US$20 million to fly to the International Space Station aboard a Russian Soyuz. His eight-day trip opened the door to privately funded spaceflight.

events.title: The Columbia disaster
events.description: Columbia broke apart during re-entry over Texas, killing all seven crew. Foam that struck the left wing during launch had breached its heat shield, and the investigation led to the Shuttle's retirement in 2011.

events.title: Shenzhou 5: China's first astronaut
events.description: Yang Liwei orbited Earth 14 times aboard Shenzhou 5, making China the third country to launch a person into space on its own. It laid the foundation for China's Tiangong space station.

events.title: Spirit and Opportunity land on Mars
events.description: The twin Mars Exploration Rovers landed three weeks apart, on 4 and 25 January. Designed for 90 days, Opportunity kept driving until 2018 and covered more than 45 km (28 miles), finding clear evidence of past liquid water.

events.title: SpaceShipOne, the first private spaceflight
events.description: Test pilot Mike Melvill flew SpaceShipOne above 100 km, the first privately funded human spaceflight. Two more flights that autumn won the US$10 million Ansari X Prize.

events.title: Cassini arrives at Saturn
events.description: Cassini fired its main engine for 96 minutes and became the first spacecraft to orbit Saturn. Over 13 years it discovered geysers of water ice erupting from the small moon Enceladus.

events.title: Huygens lands on Titan
events.description: ESA's Huygens probe parachuted through the orange haze of Saturn's largest moon and landed on its surface, the most distant landing ever made. It revealed river channels and shorelines carved by liquid methane.
events.imageCredit: ESA / NASA / JPL / University of Arizona

events.title: Pluto becomes a dwarf planet
events.description: The International Astronomical Union (IAU) adopted its first formal definition of a planet, and Pluto, which has not cleared its orbit of other bodies, was reclassified as a dwarf planet. The decision is still argued about, including by some planetary scientists.

events.title: Falcon 1 reaches orbit
events.description: After three failures, SpaceX's fourth Falcon 1 became the first privately developed liquid-fuelled rocket to reach Earth orbit. The company later said it had money for only one more try.

events.title: Chandrayaan-1 goes to the Moon
events.description: India's first lunar mission launched from Sriharikota and entered orbit around the Moon. Its NASA-built Moon Mineralogy Mapper detected the signature of water and hydroxyl spread across the lunar surface.

events.title: Kepler starts counting planets
events.description: The Kepler space telescope stared at one patch of sky, watching for the tiny dimming of stars as planets crossed in front of them. It confirmed more than 2,600 planets and showed that planets outnumber stars in our galaxy.

events.title: Hayabusa returns asteroid dust
events.description: Despite failed thrusters, a fuel leak and weeks of lost contact, JAXA's Hayabusa returned its capsule to the Australian outback. It carried the first particles ever collected from an asteroid's surface, from Itokawa.

events.title: The last Space Shuttle lands
events.description: Atlantis rolled to a stop at Kennedy Space Center at the end of STS-135, closing 30 years and 135 missions of the Space Shuttle programme. For the next nine years American astronauts flew to orbit on Russian Soyuz spacecraft.

events.title: Dragon berths at the ISS
events.description: SpaceX's Dragon became the first commercial spacecraft to berth with the International Space Station. It opened an era in which NASA buys cargo, and later crew, transport as a service.

events.title: Curiosity's sky-crane landing
events.description: The car-sized Curiosity rover was lowered into Gale Crater on cables from a rocket-powered 'sky crane'. It found that ancient Mars had long-lived lakes with the chemical ingredients life needs.

events.title: Voyager 1 enters interstellar space
events.description: Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause, where the solar wind gives way to the gas between the stars, the first human-made object to do so. Scientists confirmed the crossing a year later from the density of the surrounding plasma.

events.title: Chang'e 3 and the Yutu rover
events.description: Chang'e 3 landed in Mare Imbrium with the Yutu rover, the first soft landing on the Moon since Luna 24 in 1976. China became the third country to soft-land on the Moon.

events.title: Mangalyaan reaches Mars
events.description: The Mars Orbiter Mission made the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) the first agency to reach Mars orbit on its first attempt. It cost about US$74 million, famously less than some Hollywood space films.

events.title: Philae lands on a comet
events.description: Philae, released by ESA's Rosetta, made the first landing on a comet nucleus, 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko. Its anchoring harpoons failed and it bounced into a shadowed crevice, but it still returned data for about 60 hours.

events.title: New Horizons flies past Pluto
events.description: After a nine-and-a-half-year journey, New Horizons passed 12,500 km above Pluto. It revealed a heart-shaped plain of nitrogen ice, mountains of water ice and a blue, hazy atmosphere.

events.title: Gravitational waves detected
events.description: The two detectors of the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory (LIGO) caught ripples in space-time from two black holes merging about 1.3 billion light-years away. Announced in February 2016, the detection confirmed a century-old prediction of Einstein's and won the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics.

events.title: A Falcon 9 booster lands
events.description: After launching eleven ORBCOMM satellites, a Falcon 9 first stage flew back to Cape Canaveral and landed upright, the first orbital-class booster to do so. Reused boosters have since cut launch costs, and some have flown more than 20 times.

events.title: Juno enters orbit around Jupiter
events.description: Juno fired its engine for 35 minutes and slipped into a polar orbit around Jupiter, running on solar power farther from the Sun than any spacecraft before it. It has mapped Jupiter's deep interior, polar cyclones and enormous magnetic field.

events.title: Cassini's Grand Finale
events.description: Nearly out of fuel, Cassini dived into Saturn's atmosphere after 22 orbits threading the gap between the planet and its rings. The deliberate end protected Enceladus and Titan from contamination by microbes from Earth.

events.title: Falcon Heavy's first flight
events.description: The first Falcon Heavy, then the most powerful rocket in service, sent a Tesla Roadster into an orbit around the Sun that reaches beyond Mars. Its two side boosters touched down side by side at Cape Canaveral seconds apart.

events.title: Chang'e 4 lands on the far side
events.description: Chang'e 4 made the first soft landing on the far side of the Moon, in Von Kármán crater, and deployed the Yutu-2 rover. Because the far side never faces Earth, it talked to home through the Queqiao relay satellite.

events.title: The first image of a black hole
events.description: The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT), radio dishes around the world linked into one Earth-sized telescope, revealed the shadow of the black hole in galaxy M87. The ring's size matched the prediction of Einstein's general relativity.

events.title: Crew Dragon Demo-2
events.description: Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley flew to the International Space Station aboard SpaceX's Crew Dragon, the first crewed orbital launch from US soil since 2011. It was the first time a private company carried astronauts to orbit.

events.title: Hayabusa2 returns pieces of Ryugu
events.description: Hayabusa2's capsule landed in the Australian outback with about 5.4 g of material from asteroid Ryugu, including grains from beneath the surface. The samples contain amino acids and water-bearing minerals.

events.title: Chang'e 5 returns lunar samples
events.description: Chang'e 5 brought back 1,731 g of lunar rock and soil, the first Moon samples returned to Earth since Luna 24 in 1976. They showed that volcanoes were active on the Moon about 2 billion years ago, later than many models predicted.

events.title: Perseverance lands in Jezero Crater
events.description: Perseverance landed in an ancient lake bed, steering around hazards with terrain-relative navigation. It is collecting sealed rock cores that could one day be brought back to Earth.

events.title: Ingenuity flies on Mars
events.description: The 1.8 kg Ingenuity helicopter rose 3 m (10 ft) above Jezero Crater and hovered for about 30 seconds, the first powered, controlled flight on another planet. Built for five test flights, it flew 72 times.

events.title: Tianhe: China's space station begins
events.description: A Long March 5B launched Tianhe, the core module of the Tiangong space station. The three-module station was completed in 2022 and hosts rotating crews of three.

events.title: Zhurong rover lands on Mars
events.description: Tianwen-1's lander touched down in Utopia Planitia and released the Zhurong rover, making China the second country to operate a rover on Mars. Tianwen-1 was the first mission to orbit, land and rove on a single first attempt.

events.title: The James Webb Space Telescope launches
events.description: An Ariane 5 launched the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) from French Guiana; its 6.5 m gold-coated mirror unfolded on the way to the second Lagrange point (L2), 1.5 million km from Earth. Its first full-colour images were released in July 2022.
events.imageCredit: Webb's First Deep Field · NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI

events.title: DART moves an asteroid
events.description: The Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) slammed into the 160 m moonlet Dimorphos at about 6.1 km/s. The impact shortened its orbit around its parent asteroid by about 33 minutes, the first test of a technique for defending Earth from an asteroid.

events.title: Artemis I flies around the Moon
events.description: The first Space Launch System (SLS) sent an uncrewed Orion capsule on a 25-day flight around the Moon. Orion flew farther from Earth than any spacecraft built for humans before it and splashed down on 11 December.

events.title: JUICE launches for Jupiter's moons
events.description: An Ariane 5 launched ESA's Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (JUICE) on an eight-year journey to Jupiter. It is designed to become the first spacecraft to orbit a moon other than our own, Ganymede.

events.title: Starship's first integrated flight
events.description: Starship, the largest and most powerful rocket ever flown, lifted off from Starbase, Texas. Several engines failed and the vehicle was destroyed about four minutes in, but its data shaped the flight tests that followed.

events.title: Chandrayaan-3 lands near the south pole
events.description: Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander touched down closer to the Moon's south pole than any mission before it. India became the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon, and the Pragyan rover confirmed sulphur in the soil.

events.title: OSIRIS-REx delivers asteroid Bennu
events.description: A capsule from OSIRIS-REx parachuted into the Utah desert with rock and dust collected from asteroid Bennu in 2020. The 121.6 g sample, the largest ever returned from an asteroid, contains water-bearing minerals and organic molecules.

events.title: SLIM's pinpoint landing
events.description: JAXA's Smart Lander for Investigating Moon (SLIM) set down within tens of metres of its target, though an engine problem left it resting on its nose. Japan became the fifth country to soft-land on the Moon.

events.title: Odysseus, the first commercial Moon landing
events.description: Intuitive Machines' Odysseus became the first privately built spacecraft to land on the Moon, and the first American landing since 1972. It tipped onto its side at touchdown but still returned data.

events.title: Chang'e 6 returns far-side samples
events.description: Chang'e 6 brought back 1,935.3 g of rock and soil from the South Pole–Aitken basin, the first samples ever collected on the Moon's far side. The lander relayed its work through the Queqiao-2 satellite.

events.title: Polaris Dawn: the first commercial spacewalk
events.description: Jared Isaacman and Sarah Gillis leaned out of an open Crew Dragon hatch in SpaceX-designed suits, the first spacewalk by private astronauts. Earlier the crew reached about 1,400 km, the highest crewed Earth orbit since Apollo.

events.title: Starship's booster is caught
events.description: On Starship's fifth flight test, the 71 m Super Heavy booster flew back to its launch tower and was caught by a pair of mechanical arms nicknamed 'chopsticks'. Catching boosters is meant to allow rapid reuse without landing legs.

events.title: Europa Clipper launches
events.description: A Falcon Heavy launched Europa Clipper, NASA's largest planetary spacecraft, toward Jupiter's moon Europa, with arrival planned for 2030. It will investigate whether the ocean beneath Europa's ice could support life.

events.title: Parker Solar Probe grazes the Sun
events.description: Parker Solar Probe passed 6.1 million km (3.8 million miles) above the Sun's surface at about 692,000 km/h (430,000 mph), the closest and fastest any human-made object has flown. It is sampling the corona where the solar wind is born.

events.title: New Glenn reaches orbit
events.description: Blue Origin's New Glenn reached orbit on its first flight from Cape Canaveral, carrying a test version of its Blue Ring spacecraft platform. The booster was lost during its attempted landing at sea.

events.title: Blue Ghost lands in Mare Crisium
events.description: Firefly Aerospace's Blue Ghost Mission 1 landed upright and worked through a full lunar day, the first fully successful commercial Moon landing. It carried ten NASA science and technology payloads.

events.title: Artemis II: humans return to the Moon
events.description: Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and the Canadian Space Agency's (CSA) Jeremy Hansen flew around the Moon in Orion, the first crewed lunar voyage since 1972 and the first to carry a woman, a person of colour and a non-American. They reached 406,771 km (252,756 miles) from Earth, breaking Apollo 13's record, and splashed down off San Diego on 10 April.
